source: UNICEF Niger Humanitarian Situation Report, September 2017
processing_notes: Source states: 'Gaya department, considered a hotspot for cholera, which was the only department in Niger in 2016 to register some few cholera cases, and which is bordering Kebbi region, one of the most affected by cholera in Nigeria in 2017.' - interpreted as 38 sCh cases, 6 deaths. Derived attribution: UNICEF states Gaya department (Dosso) was the ONLY department with cholera in 2016, so the whole national 2016 count (WHO annual 38 cases/6 deaths; JHU UNICEF weekly national 18+12+8 = 38 in 17 Oct-6 Nov 2016) is assigned to Gaya; period = 13 Oct (onset at CSI Belande per ANP, AI row 310) to 6 Nov 2016 (last JHU weekly case). Conf 0.6 (combination of two sources). Contains AI row 310 (Dosso region 13-26 Oct 2016, 23 cases at CSI Belande) - do not sum. Provincial subset - do not sum with national row (JHU 2016 annual 38/6 and weekly rows).
retracted_reason: Superseded by Agent 2's own better evidence: UNICEF Niger sitrep Oct 2016 gives the direct regional figure (2 health districts of Dosso region, 38 suspected cases/11 deaths at 31 Oct 2016), so the derived Gaya-only attribution (38/6 from the 2017 'only department' statement + WHO national annual) is withdrawn.
